responsibility: Provides rustc’s front-end parsing layer that turns Rust source text into parser-ready token streams and ASTs with diagnostics and attribute checking. At the crate root, `lib.rs` exposes the main parsing entry points for files, strings, and token streams, constructs `Parser` instances, offers helpers such as fatal parse error emission, synthetic token-stream creation from AST nodes, and `cfg_attr` input parsing, and ties together the crate’s lexer and parser APIs. The `lexer` module performs source-to-token processing: it reads raw text into validated tokens and nested token trees, recovers delimiters, translates literal unescape failures into diagnostics, and detects confusing unicode characters so the parser receives normalized, recoverable token streams. The `parser` module then implements the token-stream-to-AST parser itself, maintaining shared parser state and recovery infrastructure while parsing attributes, items, modules, statements, expressions, patterns, types, paths, generics, and macro nonterminal fragments, along with ambiguity resolution, placeholder construction, token capture, and parser-stage recovery needed by later compiler phases. `errors.rs` defines the structured syntax and attribute diagnostics emitted by the lexer, parser, and attribute validation code. Finally, `validate_attr.rs` performs post-parse validation of attribute meta-syntax by converting attributes to `MetaItem` form, enforcing delimiter, literal, builtin-template, and unsafe-usage rules, and emitting or buffering diagnostics for malformed attributes. Together, these pieces give the compiler its syntax-analysis crate: lexing source, parsing Rust grammar into AST form, reporting syntax problems, and validating attributes before later compilation stages proceed.
